chunks: Abdul-Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdous al-Naysabouri al-Attar, may Allah be pleased with him, told us: He said, Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba told us, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naisabouri, from Hisham ibn Ahmad al-Yarbou'i, from Abdullah ibn Fadl, from his father, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both), from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family, forbade muka'ama and mukama'a. Muka'ama is that a man kisses a man, and mukama'a is that he hugs him while there is no robe between them for other than necessity.

key_terms.مَكْعَمَة: Kissing (specifically between men in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between muka'ama and mukama'a in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith provides precise juristic definitions for *muka'ama* (kissing) and *mukama'a* (close embrace without a garment), distinguishing them from general affection by highlighting the element of modesty and potential impropriety. The ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *satr* (covering) and *haya* (modesty) in physical interactions, serving as a foundational text for understanding the boundaries of permissible intimacy in Islamic social etiquette.
